root.name: Four Knights Game: Gunsberg Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. a3

overview: White plays a quiet 4.a3 to stop ...Bb4 and keep a flexible set-up, usually following with Bc4 or d3 and h3. Black can respond with ...d5 or ...d6 and equalises easily, and the game is a slow Italian-style manoeuvring one. It is a harmless sideline that avoids the main Four Knights theory.

white_ideas.idea: Stop ...Bb4, then play Bc4 or d3 and h3, aiming for a quiet Italian-like development.
Meet ...d5 with exd5 Nxd5 and Nxd5 Qxd5 for simplified play.

black_ideas.idea: Strike with ...d5 to equalise at once.
Play ...d6 and ...Be7 or ...g6, a solid development with a symmetrical structure.

typical_structures.structure: Symmetrical e4/e5 centre with both sides' knights on c3/c6 and f3/f6.

character.notes: Slow, quiet development with no forcing lines.

level.notes: Simple ideas but gives White nothing special.

sublines_that_differ.name: Provincial Opening
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. a3 d6 5. h3
sublines_that_differ.how: A quiet set-up with h3 and d3 in the style of the Italian.

character.reason: Quiet symmetrical play with no forcing lines.

level.reason: Easy ideas but not a first repertoire.

plans.reason: Mirror-image pawns and a slow fight.
